sentences.zh: 今被堂侄伯強進狀，請貨宅召市人馬，以討吐蕃。

translations.literal: Now his paternal cousin Boqiang has submitted a petition requesting to sell the residence and hire market men and horses to campaign against Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Now his paternal cousin Boqiang has submitted a petition requesting to sell the residence and hire market men and horses to campaign against Tibet.

sentences.zh: 一開此門，恐滋不逞。

translations.literal: Once this door is opened, I fear it will breed the unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once this door is opened, I fear it will encourage reckless opportunism.

sentences.zh: 討賊自有國計，豈資僥幸之徒？

translations.literal: Suppressing rebels has its own state plan—how can it rely on men of lucky chance?
translations.idiomatic: Suppressing rebels follows the state's own plan. How can it rely on opportunists?

sentences.zh: 且毀棄義門，虧損風教，望少責罰，亦可懲勸。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to destroy a gate of righteousness damages moral instruction; I hope for a light punishment, which may also serve as warning and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, to destroy a gate of righteousness damages moral instruction. I hope for a light punishment, which may also serve as warning and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 上可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 先時，韓滉自浙西入覲，朝廷委政待之，至於調兵食，籠鹽鐵，勾官吏贓罰，鋤豪強兼並，上悉仗焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Huang came from Zhexi to attend court; the court entrusted him with government and relied on him for adjusting troops and provisions, controlling salt and iron, investigating official corruption and punishments, and uprooting powerful families' encroachments—the emperor wholly depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Huang came from Zhexi to attend court. The court entrusted him with government and relied on him for adjusting troops and provisions, controlling salt and iron, investigating official corruption, and uprooting powerful families' encroachments. The emperor wholly depended on him.

sentences.zh: 每奏事，或日旰，他相充位而已，公卿救過不能暇，無敢枝梧者。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported on affairs, it sometimes lasted until sundown; the other chief ministers merely filled their posts; the high officials had no leisure to remedy their faults, and none dared resist.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reported on affairs, it sometimes lasted until sundown. The other chief ministers merely filled their posts. The high officials had no leisure to remedy their faults, and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 渾雖滉所引，心惡其專政，正色讓之曰：「先相公以狷察為相，不滿歲而罷；

translations.literal: Though Hun had been introduced by Huang, he hated his monopoly of power at heart and said sternly in rebuke: 'The former chief minister served as chief minister through narrow scrutiny and was dismissed before a year had passed;
translations.idiomatic: Though Hun had been introduced by Han Huang, he hated Huang's monopoly of power at heart and said sternly in rebuke, "The former chief minister served through narrow scrutiny and was dismissed before a year had passed;

sentences.zh: 今相公搒吏於省中至死，且非刑人之地，奈何蹈前非而又甚焉？

translations.literal: now the chief minister beats an official to death within the ministry—and this is not a place for punishing men. Why repeat the former fault and make it even worse?
translations.idiomatic: now you beat an official to death within the ministry—and this is not a place for punishing men. Why repeat the former fault and make it even worse?

sentences.zh: 專立威福，豈尊主卑臣之禮！」

translations.literal: To monopolize authority and favor—is this the ritual of honoring the ruler and lowering the minister!
translations.idiomatic: To monopolize authority and favor—is this the ritual of honoring the ruler and lowering the minister!

sentences.zh: 滉感悟愧悔，為霽威焉。

translations.literal: Huang was moved to awareness and shame and thereupon eased his severity.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang was moved to awareness and shame and thereupon eased his severity.

sentences.zh: 及白誌貞除浙西觀察使，渾奏曰：「誌貞一末吏憸人，縱稱廉謹，不當頓居重職。」

translations.literal: When Bai Zhizhen was appointed observation commissioner of Zhexi, Hun memorialized, saying: 'Zhizhen is a petty official and a treacherous man; even if he is called honest and careful, he ought not suddenly occupy a heavy post.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Zhizhen was appointed observation commissioner of Zhexi, Hun memorialized, saying, "Zhizhen is a petty official and a treacherous man. Even if he is called honest and careful, he ought not suddenly occupy a heavy post.

sentences.zh: 適遇渾以疾稱告，即日詔下。

translations.literal: It happened that Hun requested leave on grounds of illness, and the edict was issued that same day.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Hun requested leave on grounds of illness, and the edict was issued that same day.

sentences.zh: 疾間，因乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Between bouts of illness he requested to retire on account of old bones; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Between bouts of illness he requested to retire on account of old age. A gracious edict did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 其判門下，主吏白當過官，渾愀然曰：「列官分職，復更撓之，非禮法也。

translations.literal: In his oversight of the Secretariat, the chief clerk reported that he should call on officials; Hun said with a somber face: 'Officials are arrayed with divided duties—if I further interfere, that is not ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: In his oversight of the Secretariat, the chief clerk reported that he should call on officials. Hun said with a somber face, "Officials are arrayed with divided duties. If I further interfere, that is not ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 千里辭家，以幹微祿，邑主辭辦，豈慮無能，矧旌善進賢，事不在此。」

translations.literal: Having left home for a thousand li to seek a small salary, the local chief handles affairs—why worry about incapacity? Moreover, honoring good and advancing the worthy—the matter is not here.
translations.idiomatic: Having left home for a thousand li to seek a small salary, the local chief handles affairs—why worry about incapacity? Moreover, honoring good and advancing the worthy—the matter is not here.

sentences.zh: 故其年註擬，無退量者。

translations.literal: Therefore in that year's appointments, none were rejected for insufficient measure.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in that year's appointments, none were rejected for insufficient qualifications.

sentences.zh: 及渾瑊與吐蕃會盟之日，上御便殿謂宰相曰：「和戎息師，國之大計，今日將士與卿同歡。」

translations.literal: On the day when Hun Zhen allied with Tibet, the emperor attended the informal hall and told the chief ministers: 'Making peace with the barbarians and resting the armies is a great plan of state—today soldiers and ministers rejoice together with you.
translations.idiomatic: On the day when Hun Zhen allied with Tibet, the emperor attended the informal hall and told the chief ministers, "Making peace with the barbarians and resting the armies is a great plan of state. Today soldiers and ministers rejoice together with you.

sentences.zh: 馬燧前賀曰：今之一盟，百年內更無蕃寇。」

translations.literal: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying: With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui stepped forward in congratulation, saying, "With this one alliance, within a hundred years there will be no more Tibetan raids."

sentences.zh: 渾曰：「五帝無誥誓之盟，皆在季末。

translations.literal: Hun said: 'The Five Emperors had no alliances of proclamation and oath—all such came at the end of ages.
translations.idiomatic: Hun said, "The Five Emperors had no alliances of proclamation and oath. All such came at the end of ages.

sentences.zh: 今盛明之代，豈又行於夷狄！

translations.literal: In this flourishing and enlightened age, how can it again be practiced with barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: In this flourishing and enlightened age, how can it again be practiced with barbarians!

sentences.zh: 人面獸心，難以信結，今日盟約，臣竊憂之。」

translations.literal: Human faces with beast hearts—hard to bind by trust; today's alliance, your servant privately worries over it.'
translations.idiomatic: Human faces with beast hearts—they are hard to bind by trust. Your servant privately worries over today's alliance."

sentences.zh: 李晟繼言曰：「臣生長邊城，知蕃戎心，今日之事，誠如渾言。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng continued, saying: 'Your servant grew up on the frontier and knows the Tibetan mind; today's matter is truly as Hun says.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng continued, saying, "Your servant grew up on the frontier and knows the Tibetan mind. Today's matter is truly as Liu Hun says."

sentences.zh: 上變色曰：「柳渾書生，未達邊事；

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: 'Liu Hun is a bookish man and does not understand frontier affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed color and said, "Liu Hun is a bookish man and does not understand frontier affairs;

sentences.zh: 大臣智略，果亦有斯言乎！」

translations.literal: great ministers with wisdom and strategy—can there truly be such words as well!'
translations.idiomatic: great ministers with wisdom and strategy—can there truly be such words as well!"

sentences.zh: 皆頓首俯伏，遽令歸中書。

translations.literal: All knocked their heads and prostrated themselves; he immediately ordered them to return to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: All kowtowed and prostrated themselves. He immediately ordered them to return to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其夜三更，邠寧節度韓遊瑰飛驛叩苑門，奏盟會不成，將校覆沒，兵臨近鎮，上驚嘆，即遞其表以示渾。

translations.literal: That night at the third watch, Binning military governor Han Yougui sent a fast courier to knock at the park gate, reporting that the alliance meeting failed, generals and officers were wiped out, and troops pressed the nearby garrison; the emperor exclaimed in alarm and immediately forwarded the memorial to show Hun.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch, Binning military governor Han Yougui sent a fast courier to knock at the park gate, reporting that the alliance meeting failed, generals and officers were wiped out, and troops pressed the nearby garrison. The emperor exclaimed in alarm and immediately forwarded the memorial to show Liu Hun.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，臨軒慰勉渾曰：「卿文儒之士，而萬里知軍戎之情。」

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, facing the hall he comforted and encouraged Hun, saying: 'You are a literary and Confucian gentleman, yet you knew the feelings of the army a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day, facing the hall he comforted and encouraged Liu Hun, saying, "You are a literary and Confucian gentleman, yet you knew the feelings of the army a thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 自此驟加禮異。

translations.literal: From this he suddenly added special honors.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the emperor suddenly added special honors.

sentences.zh: 時張延賞與渾同列，延賞怙權矜己，而嫉渾守正，俾其所厚謂渾曰：「相公舊德，但節言於廟堂，則重位可久。」。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yanshang served in the same rank as Hun; Yanshang relied on power and prided himself on his person, yet envied Hun's uprightness; he had one he favored tell Hun, saying: 'The chief minister's old virtue—if you only restrain your words in the court hall, then a high post may last long.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Yanshang served in the same rank as Liu Hun. Yanshang relied on power and prided himself on his person, yet envied Hun's uprightness. He had one he favored tell Hun, saying, "The chief minister's old virtue—if you only restrain your words in the court hall, then a high post may last long.

sentences.zh: 渾曰：「為吾謝張相公，柳渾頭可斷，而舌不可禁也。」

translations.literal: Hun said: 'Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang—Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced.
translations.idiomatic: Hun said, "Give my thanks to Chief Minister Zhang. Liu Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced.

sentences.zh: 自是為其所擠，尋除常侍，罷知政事。

translations.literal: From this he was squeezed out by him; soon he was appointed regular attendant and relieved of participation in government.
translations.idiomatic: From this he was squeezed out by Yanshang. He was soon appointed regular attendant and relieved of participation in government.

sentences.zh: 貞元五年二月，以疾終，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Zhenyuan he died of illness at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected writings in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 渾母兄識，，篤意文章，有重名於開元、天寶間，與蕭穎士、元德秀、劉迅相亞。

translations.literal: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during Kaiyuan and Tianbao, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's elder maternal brother Shi was devoted to literature and had a great reputation during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, ranking alongside Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun.

sentences.zh: 其練理創端往往詣極，當時作者，鹹伏其簡拔，而趣尚辨博。

translations.literal: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost; writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: In refining principles and opening beginnings he often reached the utmost. Writers of the time all submitted to his concise elevation, yet his bent favored disputation and breadth.

sentences.zh: 渾亦善為文，然趨時向功，非沈思之所及。

translations.literal: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.
translations.idiomatic: Hun also wrote well, yet he bent to the times and sought achievement—not what deep reflection could reach.

sentences.zh: 渾警辯，好諧謔放達，與人交，豁然無隱。

translations.literal: Hun was alert in debate, fond of jest and free openness; in dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was alert in debate and fond of jest and free openness. In dealing with people he was expansive and hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 性節儉，不治產業，官至丞相，假宅而居。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates; though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and did not manage estates. Though he reached chief minister, he borrowed a residence to live in.

sentences.zh: 罷相數日，則命親族尋勝，宴醉方歸，陶陶然忘其黜免。

translations.literal: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of leaving the chief ministry he would order kin to seek scenic spots, feast until drunk before returning, and forget his dismissal in contentment.

sentences.zh: 時李勉、盧翰皆退罷居第，相謂曰：「吾輩方柳宜城，悉為拘俗之人也。」

translations.literal: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences; they said to each other: 'Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Mian and Lu Han had both retired and lived at their residences. They said to each other, "Compared with Liu of Yicheng, we are all people bound by convention."

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：張鎰、蕭復、柳渾，節行才能訏謨亮直，皆足相明主，平泰階，而盧杞忌之於前，延賞排之於後，管仲有言：「任君子，使小人間之，害霸也。」

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist a enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway; yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said: 'Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Zhang Yi, Xiao Fu, and Liu Hun—in integrity, conduct, talent, and outspoken, bright uprightness—all were sufficient to assist an enlightened ruler and level the grand stairway. Yet Lu Qi envied them before and Yanshang excluded them after. Guan Zhong said, "Employ the gentleman and let petty men come between—this harms hegemony.

sentences.zh: 德宗黜賢相，位奸臣，致硃泚、懷光之亂，是失其人也，豈尤其時哉！

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang—this was losing the right men; how can one blame the times alone!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong dismissed worthy chief ministers and placed treacherous ministers in rank, bringing about the disorders of Zhu Ci and Huai Guang. This was losing the right men. How can one blame the times alone!

sentences.zh: 河清歿於王事，乃顯忠貞；

translations.literal: Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Heqing died in royal service and thereby displayed loyalty and steadfastness;

sentences.zh: 從一舉自奸人，固宜循默。

translations.literal: Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have followed silence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congyi was raised by treacherous men and properly ought to have kept silent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：得人則興，失人則亡。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Gain the right men and flourish; lose them and perish.

sentences.zh: 鎰、復、渾去，宗社其殃。

translations.literal: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi, Fu, and Hun departed, the altars of state met calamity.
